items.reason: No server route or database function is called from this area: no web request, no Supabase client, no remote call. Every read and write goes to the phone's own on-device database or to on-phone settings storage.

Apps cannot read these tables from the server at all: every table this area touches (sessions, sets, routines, folders, exercise settings, body measurements, photos, profile extras) lives only in the phone's own database, and none of them exists in the server migrations, so there is no gym-to-gym boundary for a server test to prove. No database test file is tied to this area.
Rule applied: no server table is touched by this area, so no table lacks a cross-gym test and no finding is due.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code and the server migration list were read.
The secrets scan has no key pattern hits in this area, and a search of the area's files for keys, tokens and web addresses found only the profile-link helper that adds https:// to a typed link.
No AI or paid-service key is read or used by any file in this area; nothing here calls a paid service.
No sign-in, PIN or session handling in the workout data and settings code.

Every typed value (routine and workout names, notes, bio, link, search) reaches the phone database only as a bound value. The few queries built from text use fixed column or table names from the code; the one that loops over table names (merging two exercises) takes them from the database's own list and skips any odd name. The profile link only keeps http or https addresses with a normal host, so a script link cannot be saved.
Nothing here uploads. Custom exercise media, workout photos and the profile photo are kept as file locations on the phone; workout photos are left out of the Drive backup on purpose.
No gym page, join code or shareable link is made or opened here; the only link is the member's own profile link, which they type.

The area's only outside libraries are the state store and the phone settings storage; neither has an alert in the dependency scan. The repo-wide gap (automatic dependency alerts switched off) is already recorded and reused here.
